newsitem.title: CHINA: Foreign firms eyeing China power project - report.
newsitem.headline: Foreign firms eyeing China power project - report.

text.p: A number of foreign companies and consortia have expressed interest in bidding for a build-operate-transfer (BOT) power project in central China, the official China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.
The Hunan Changsha Power Plant is one of the few BOT projects approved so far by the Chinese government, the newspaper said.

Construction is scheduled to begin in 1998 and the plant will be transferred to China in 20 years, the newspaper said, quoting Xiao Lejian, executive vice president of the BOT International Engineering Development Co Ltd.
The plant, in central Hunan province, will have two 350-megawatt coal-fired generators, the newspaper said.

The foreign groups or companies that have taken bidding specifications include: Britain's National Power, a consortium between Britain's PowerGen and Japan's Itochu Corp, and a consortium between Electricite de France and GEC Alsthom.
Other consortia or firms that have expressed an interest include Japan's Mitsubishi Corp, Japan's Mitsui & Co Ltd and a U.S. consortium involving Exxon Corp.
The deadline for submitting bids is September 25, Xiao said. -- Shanghai newsroom (86-21) 6279-7004
